name: 甲賀米粉たい焼き 姫路城前店 (Koga Komeko Taiyaki Himejijoumae-ten)

claims.text: No wheat is used anywhere in the production process — the dough is 100% rice flour. Cross-contamination from wheat within this shop is very low risk by design, though no formal certification is published.
No soy sauce or wheat-containing condiments are used. This is a sweet pastry shop; soy sauce is not part of any product.
Egg and dairy are present in all products (dough contains egg, cow's milk, and soy milk; custard filling adds more egg and dairy). There is no vegan-safe option on the menu.

No published allergy-handling protocol found for this location. The concept is wheat-free by design, which simplifies wheat-allergy inquiries, but staff are not confirmed to speak English or handle complex allergy queries in writing.

Entire menu is wheat-free by concept — rice flour is the only flour used in all products, making this a naturally safe environment for wheat-allergic diners without needing to scrutinize individual items.
Allergen declarations on chain products list only egg and dairy — wheat is absent from the ingredient list entirely.

name: MIL bake (米粉専門店ミルベイク)

claims.text: 「工房では小麦粉を使用しません」— no wheat flour is used anywhere in the workshop, so flour cross-contact is not a factor.
All bread is described as 米粉100%; breads are 「小麦・乳・卵・ナッツ不使用」 per the shop.
Bakery — no soy sauce in products. 豆乳ロールパン contains soy milk (not soy sauce); soy-sensitive guests should note it.
Egg and dairy are used in the same wheat-free workshop for sweets and cakes; vegans should stick to the plain 米粉 breads listed as egg/dairy-free.

Owner is herself a wheat-allergic former pâtissier who built the shop specifically for wheat allergy / intolerance / medically wheat-restricted customers; fruit allergies and preferences accommodated on request.
Entirely wheat-free rice-flour workshop run by an allergy-affected owner — 「なるべく身体に負担のない材料で」, using domestic rice flour, potato starch, rice oil, beet sugar and sea salt.
Breads free of wheat, dairy, egg and nuts — usable by celiac and vegan guests alike.

name: Baker theta (ベイカー シータ)

claims.text: Allergy-focused source explicitly advises confirming cross-contamination with the shop before visiting: 「コンタミについては訪問前に必ずお店に確認をお取りください」.
The entire bakery is 米粉100％ with no wheat flour used (小麦粉不使用), so there is no wheat on the premises to cross-contaminate.

This is a rice-flour bakery, not a restaurant; soy sauce is not a featured ingredient and no wheat-based seasoning claims were found. Savory items such as mentaiko French and shio-koji chicken should still be checked for wheat-containing sauces.
Egg (平飼い卵のサンド), dairy (butter breads, cheese items) and fish (明太フランス) are handled in the same bakery, so vegan customers should ask about shared surfaces.
Each product is individually labelled with allergen flags such as 卵不使用・乳不使用・小麦不使用 (egg/dairy/wheat-free), making allergen status easy to verify at the shop.
100% rice-flour bakery with no wheat flour used anywhere — 「米粉100％の身体に優しいパン」— which is unusually safe for celiacs.
Additive-free concept catering explicitly to egg and dairy allergies, with per-item allergen labelling.
Facility uses only domestic rice flour and no wheat flour at all, fundamentally eliminating cross-contamination from equipment and utensils.
Shop describes itself as a fully gluten-free rice-flour bread specialist (完全グルテンフリー米粉パン専門店).
Bakery, not a restaurant; savory toasts (tuna, mentaiko garlic) may use seasonings/sauces — celiacs should confirm those specific items, though plain breads carry no wheat.
Cheese and chocolate varieties contain dairy; savory toasts contain fish. Plain breads are egg- and dairy-free.
Positioned explicitly for the three major food allergies (wheat, egg, dairy); allergy-aware operation.
Entirely wheat-free premises — no wheat baking on site, the strongest cross-contact protection a bakery can offer.
Nationwide online shop lets celiacs order the same GF breads remotely.
Bakes only with rice flour; no wheat flour used anywhere, so cross-contact risk in the workshop is minimal.
Self-described Vegan & Gluten-free 工房 making sweets without wheat flour, egg, dairy or white sugar.
Sweets-only shop; no soy sauce / savory wheat seasonings involved.
Fully plant-based — no eggs, dairy or animal products in the baked goods.
Mission is snacks anyone can eat safely, including allergy sufferers; featured by allergy-focused guide alleco.
Entirely wheat-free premises using only rice flour — strong protection against gluten cross-contact.
Nationwide shipping (free over ¥4,500) for the same vegan GF sweets.
They fry the karaage in separate, dedicated oil so there is no cross-contact.
The entire menu is free of wheat, egg, and dairy, so there are no gluten-containing dishes prepared in the same kitchen.
They use gluten-free (wheat-free) soy sauce; seasonings are also wheat-free.
The owner, a former dietician, developed the recipes and is careful about seasonings being wheat-free.
Staff are very knowledgeable about celiac disease and changed their practices (adopting gluten-free soy sauce) after learning from a celiac customer.
The owner worked about ten years as a dietician across schools, hospitals, and corporate cafeterias before opening the cafe.
Described as probably the best place for celiacs to eat anywhere on Miyajima Island, with carefully prepared, excellent karaage.
All meals are wheat-, egg-, and dairy-free and recommended for those seeking a gluten-free meal.
The entire menu is wheat-free, so there are no wheat-flour products in the kitchen, but no formal celiac cross-contamination protocol has been published.
All sweets and food are fully plant-based with no animal products on the menu, eliminating dairy/egg cross-contact at the recipe level.

The owner explicitly verifies that plant milks and ingredients contain no wheat, choosing only wheat-free products; a documented anecdote describes a parent being told their allergic child could safely choose anything in the shop.
A dedicated plant-based and gluten-free cafe — every item is made without eggs, dairy, or wheat, so vegan and gluten-free guests can order anything on the menu.
Sweets are also made without white sugar, artificial coloring, or preservatives.

name: Komeko Udon Undo (米粉うどん製麺所 undo／あんど)

claims.text: Dedicated rice-flour udon operation using 100% domestic rice flour; the shop states 「小麦粉不使用」 (no wheat flour used). No formal cross-contact/allergen protocol has been published, so confirm equipment is not shared with any wheat item.
The shop states 「出汁やタレなどもすべてグルテンフリー」 (the dashi, sauces and tare are all gluten-free), implying wheat-free soy/tare; confirm the specific bowl's tare is the gluten-free one.
Vegan options exist (vegetable okonomiyaki ~¥1,200), but shared broths may contain fish dashi; vegans should confirm the broth.
The business was created specifically to serve gluten-free and vegan tourist demand, so staff are accustomed to allergen questions; no written allergen policy published.
100% domestic rice-flour noodles; all dashi and sauces advertised as gluten-free — a genuine celiac-safe savory meal.
